identityReview: Matched Wiki inventor and Kent Beck collaborator across original technical reports, Purdue, IEEE interview and podcast. Birth May 26, 1949 agrees between IEEE biographical box, IT History Society and Wikipedia. Birth city conflicts: IEEE says Chicago, Wikipedia Michigan City; neither asserted.

corrections: No assertion Cunningham invented HyperCard. O’Reilly search biography makes this error and retains an outdated AboutUs CTO title; excluded from dossier sources.

WikiWikiWeb is distinct from Wikipedia. March 25, 1995 public launch supported by IT History Society and 30th-anniversary podcast; 1994 development and earlier private testing are separate. C2 WikiHistory endpoint exposed only a JavaScript notice, not inspected article text.

Purdue identifies interdisciplinary engineering bachelor’s and computer-science master’s. Anniversary profile assigns 1978 to bachelor’s; Wikipedia ambiguously says graduating in 1978. IEEE interview describes extended campus employment before Tektronix in 1978. Separate degree completion years remain unconfirmed and are omitted; do not manufacture a contradictory exact year.

IEEE biographical box says Chicago while Wikipedia says Michigan City. Exact birth date corroborated, specific city omitted. IT History Society legacy author is unknown and is not independent primary birth documentation.

Retain Kent Beck as coauthor of both original papers and Christopher Alexander as antecedent of pattern-language ideas. September 17, 1987 is technical-report date, not conference occurrence. CRC source says October 1989 proceedings and October 1–6 conference; month precision retained.

March 26, 1992 is manuscript date on WyCash report, not a claim about the OOPSLA conference date. Debt metaphor concerns incremental development and consolidation, not blanket endorsement of careless code.
Manifesto has seventeen coauthors at the February 11–13, 2001 meeting. Cunningham is not its sole author and agile is not synonymous with Scrum.

2011 IndieWeb notes identify M. Edward Borasky as collaborator. Current project description credits open-source community maintenance; no claim sole ongoing maintenance or verified current corporate job.

April 27, 2026 is correspondence date cited on page 12 of the public paper, not publication date. No personal messages accessed. November 2026 MediaWiki conference listings name Cunningham only as a notable past speaker; not proof of attending that event.

March 25, 2025 podcast is an episode release date, not verified recording date; description read, no claim to have listened to the audio. FIT site failed to open and no unsupported exact launch event was included.
